title: Legal Services Court Reporter (MGySgt to Cpl) NMOS (4421), SJA to CMC #
raw_text:
3. MOS 4422, Legal Services Court Reporter (MGySgt to Cpl) NMOS (4421), SJA
to CMC #

    a. Summary. Legal Services Court Reporters are responsible for the
closed mask capture, transcription, and distribution of legal proceedings and
assembly of typewritten, summarized or verbatim, transcripts. Reporters
record the proceedings of special and general courts-martial, formal
investigations, administrative boards, and other similar bodies; prepare or
supervise preparation and assembly of typewritten, summarized or verbatim,
transcripts; and review records of proceedings for administrative
completeness and technical accuracy.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must hold primary MOS 4421.

        (2) Must be able to type a minimum of 30 words per minute on a 5-
minute typing test.

        (3) Must be an NCO at the time of application. Lance Corporals with
one year time on station may apply with the recommendation of their
supervisor.

    c. Requirements. Marines assigned the NMOS 4422 must first attend and
complete the Legal Services Court Reporter Course (N05LN31) at Naval Justice
School, Naval Station, Newport, RI. This is an approximately 12 week course
in closed-mask capture and speech recognition transcription methods. Upon
successful completion of the course, students will be sworn as Court-Martial
Court Reporters.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (bh), Legal Services Training and Readiness Manual.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Court Reporters 23-2091.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   None.

# The Base Education Center administers and grades the tests for prerequisite
(2). If there isn't an education center where the Marine is located, tests
will be mailed to the Command.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
